aic:36660.summary: On one face of this gold coin Christ sits frontally on a throne, haloed, holding the book of the Gospels, with a Latin legend proclaiming him King of rulers. On the other face the Virgin crowns the Emperor Romanos III Argyros, who holds a cross-topped orb. Passed from hand to hand across the empire, such coins proclaimed that the emperor ruled under Christ, the true King.
facts: Romanos III Argyros reigned 1028–1034; the Art Institute notes that he died possibly at the hands, or on the order, of his wife Zoe.
The legend around Christ reads IhS XIS REX REGNANTIUM ('Jesus Christ, King of those who reign').
The coin is about 2.5 cm in diameter.

aic:36660.notes: Place given by the museum as 'Istanbul'; changed to the historical name Constantinople. The museum's text says Christ holds the Gospel book in his right hand, but in the photograph he holds it in his left, with the right hand at his breast.
